scenarios.name: rules_from_the_instruction_file_shape_a_commit
scenarios.summary: A commit task: the user's rules reach the agent through the instruction file setup wrote, so the commit carries no AI attribution and the agent asks before pushing.

args: No AI attribution in commits: no Co-Authored-By or Generated-with lines
Commits in the user's repositories carry no trace of AI tools: no Co-Authored-By trailer and no 'Generated with' line naming an AI tool or model; the user is the sole author.
Push only after the user says so; ask first
Commit locally, then ask before pushing: push, publish or tag only after the user's explicit go-ahead.

sessions.prompt: Add the line 'Run `make docs` to build the documentation.' to README.md and commit the change.

answer.matches: want me to push|(say|tell me|let me know) if you want|shall I push|push[^.\n]*\?

scenarios.name: claude_records_through_user_memory_with_auto_memory_on
scenarios.summary: With Claude Code's own auto memory on, a new global preference is recorded through record, with a title and the real origin, and nothing lands in Claude's memory files; a lesson about the repository goes to record with project scope.

sessions.prompt: From now on, in every project: write commit messages in the imperative mood, with a short body that explains why. Remember this for future sessions. One more thing, about this repository only: its integration tests need `just test-integration`, because plain `cargo test` skips them.

scenarios.name: codex_records_through_user_memory
scenarios.summary: In Codex, a new global preference is recorded through record, with a title and the real origin.

sessions.prompt: From now on, in every project: write commit messages in the imperative mood, with a short body that explains why. Remember this for future sessions.

scenarios.name: a_rule_is_read_before_it_is_applied
scenarios.summary: A rule whose title leaves out a condition that matters: the agent reads it in full before answering, and follows the condition.

args: Use tabs for indentation in Go code
Use tabs for indentation in Go code, except in files under gen/: those are generated and keep the generator's formatting, so never reformat them by hand.

sessions.prompt: I'm about to reindent gen/parser.go with tabs so it matches the rest of our Go code. Any reason not to? Just answer; don't change anything.

scenarios.name: instruction_files_alone_carry_the_rules
scenarios.summary: With the hooks off, the instruction file alone carries the rules: the agent follows one and records a new preference through user-memory.

args: Name branches type/short-description in lowercase with hyphens, like fix/login-timeout or feat/csv-export.

sessions.prompt: What should I name the branch for fixing the broken PDF export? Also, from now on I want short answers, three sentences at most, in every project. Please remember that.

scenarios.name: a_rule_recorded_in_one_session_reaches_the_next
scenarios.summary: Session A records a rule; session B, started afterwards, has it in its instruction file and applies it.

steps.prompt: From now on, in every project: whenever you write a date for me, use the ISO format YYYY-MM-DD. Please remember that.
Write one line telling the team that the release went out on March 3rd, 2027.

scenarios.name: forgetting_a_chat_removes_only_its_memories
scenarios.summary: "Forget that chat" deletes the memories carrying its origin and keeps the rest.

args: Run home lab services in rootless Podman
Run home lab services in rootless Podman
The home lab router is an OPNsense box
The home lab router is an OPNsense box

sessions.prompt: Please forget everything from the chat where we talked about my home lab setup. Keep everything else.

scenarios.name: a_running_session_hears_of_a_new_rule
scenarios.summary: Session B is running; session A records a rule; B's next prompt brings the change notice, and B reads the rule and applies it.

steps.prompt: Later I'll ask you for a short team note. For now, just reply: ready.
From now on, in every project: end every team note you write for me with the line 'Thanks, everyone.' Please remember that.
Write a two-line team note saying the nightly build is green.

hook_context.matches: Memory changed since this session last looked

scenarios.name: a_linked_repository_stays_loaded_through_compaction_and_resume
scenarios.summary: A session in a parent folder links a repository, is compacted and resumed, and still applies that repository's project rule.

args: In the notebooks repository, name data files YYYYMMDD_<topic>.parquet, with the date the data was cleaned, so they sort by date.

steps.prompt: I'll be working on the notebooks repository in this folder for the rest of this conversation. Keep its project memories loaded; nothing else to do yet, just confirm.
Today is 2027-03-03. What should I name the file for today's cleaned sales data in notebooks? Give just the file name.

scenarios.name: a_folder_without_git_gets_a_key_only_after_a_yes
scenarios.summary: A session in a folder without git hears about the work: it proposes a project key and asks, records nothing global, and sets the key only after the user's yes.

steps.prompt: I'm starting a new command-line tool in this folder; it will live at github.com/me/newapp once I push it. Keep in mind for this project: it must run on Python 3.12 only, nothing older.
Yes, use github.com/me/newapp as this folder's project key, and remember the Python note for it.

matches: ^No project: this folder has no git remote and no \.user-memory-key

scenarios.name: a_cross_project_habit_becomes_global_only_after_a_yes
scenarios.summary: A session notices a habit the user has in more than one project: it records nothing global until the user says it holds everywhere.

steps.prompt: I wrote the CHANGELOG entry for notebooks by hand this morning, and I'll write the one for this repository myself too, so leave CHANGELOG.md alone. Just tell me in one sentence what a parser-fix release usually changes.
Yes: I write changelog entries myself in every project. Please remember that.

scenarios.name: a_stated_need_to_list_repositories_is_acted_on
scenarios.summary: The user says linking the same repositories from a parent folder every time is annoying: that is the request, so the session lists both with project-id --include and says what it wrote.

steps.prompt: I keep working with the notebooks and compiler repositories from this folder, and it's annoying to link them every time.
